rendering.persona_description: Idris is a 24-year-old transgender man who works part-time stocking shelves at a hardware store while he finishes an HVAC certification at community college. He's into fixing up an old motorcycle in his spare time and keeps a running list of things he's supposed to worry less about. He's close with his younger sister but doesn't talk to his parents much these days.
rendering.clinical_context: Idris has generalized anxiety with persistent worry that's been part of his life since high school, focused mostly on money, whether he's screwing up at work, and whether people are annoyed with him even when there's no sign of it. He did a course of exposure-based treatment a while back, working on tolerating uncertainty by deliberately not checking or reassurance-seeking in situations that used to trigger it, but that ended over a year ago and he hasn't been in any treatment since.
rendering.behavioral_description: Idris talks fast when he's anxious and slow and flat when he's tired of the topic, and he'll cut himself off mid-sentence to say 'never mind, it's stupid.' He pushes back hard on anything that sounds like a script or a checklist, even when he agrees with the substance of it, and he'll say things like 'I know what I'm supposed to do' in a clipped tone when he feels cornered. He's more willing to talk about why he stopped than to hear another way to do it.

traits.profession: part-time hardware store stock clerk, HVAC certification student
traits.living_situation: shares a rented duplex with a roommate
traits.communication_register: casual, clipped when defensive, uses some self-deprecating humor
traits.help_seeking_orientation: ambivalent: sought treatment himself in the past but resisted direction once in it, and hasn't gone back since
traits.cognitive_style: quick to spiral into what-ifs, then argues himself out of them only partway, leaving him stuck between the worry and his own case against it

clinical_history.presentation: generalized anxiety disorder with chronic, free-floating worry about work performance, money, and social standing
clinical_history.history: worry has been present since roughly age 15-16, worsening during periods of financial or job instability; his first and only course of structured treatment was exposure-based work he started after his sister pushed him to go, but it ended more than a year ago.

symptoms: persistent worry about work mistakes and money
muscle tension, especially jaw and shoulders
trouble falling asleep because of running through scenarios
restlessness, hard to sit still through a full episode of worry
irritability when asked about why he stopped treatment
avoidance of situations that used to prompt checking or reassurance-seeking

affect.valence: negative, with flashes of dry humor
affect.primary_emotion: defensive frustration layered over anxious worry
